sum: A nine-day trek up the Everest trail to Pangboche, with a day walk to the expedition base camp below Ama Dablam at 4,570 m and no night above 4,000 m.

guide.note: Khumbu has not enforced the national guide requirement, and on the main trail you will not lose your way. The path from Pangboche to base camp is different: it is unsigned and splits into yak tracks on the upper pasture, and in cloud it is easy to drift into the wrong valley. A licensed guide who has been up before is worth having for that day alone.

access: The trek begins and ends with the flight to Lukla, which leaves in the early morning from Kathmandu or, in peak season, from Manthali in Ramechhap. Flights wait on the weather at Lukla, and a day's delay at either end is normal enough to plan for.

photo.a: A line of trekkers follows a trail across a steep grassy hillside towards a small stupa, with the snow peak of Ama Dablam rising ahead under a clear blue sky.
photo.c: Ama Dablam from the trail near Pangboche

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Sagarmatha park and Khumbu municipality permits
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
airport transfers; Kathmandu hotel nights in some packages

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.

transportText: Flights to Lukla and back, from Kathmandu or (in the busy months) from Manthali with a night drive to the airstrip
tips: Order a packed lunch in Pangboche the night before; there is nothing dependable to eat on the way to base camp.
Expedition camps are workplaces. Ask before you walk between the tents or take photographs, and do not expect to be fed.
Upper Pangboche is a short climb above the lodges on the main trail and has the oldest monastery in Khumbu.
Bring the cash you need from Kathmandu or Namche; there is none to be had higher up.
If cloud hides the mountain in the morning and you have a spare day, wait for the next one. The walk is about what you see at the end.

days.t: Fly to Lukla, walk to Phakding
days.note: Once the flight is in, walk down through Chheplung to the Dudh Koshi and follow it upstream to Phakding. It is a gentle afternoon, and sleeping lower than Lukla helps on the first night.
Riverside walking to the park gate at Monjo, then the steady 600 m climb from the high bridge to Namche. Ama Dablam stays hidden all day; it first appears from the ridge above Namche tomorrow.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Walk up to the Everest View Hotel for the first full view of Ama Dablam with Everest and Lhotse behind it, return through Khumjung and sleep again in Namche. Do not skip the walk; it is what makes the next days comfortable.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Ama Dablam is ahead of you along the whole balcony trail. Drop to the river at Phunki Tenga for lunch, then climb two hours through forest to the monastery, where the mountain fills the eastern skyline.

A short stage on purpose. Walk down through the forest at Deboche, cross the Imja Khola and climb gently to Pangboche. Spend the afternoon at the monastery in the upper village and pick out tomorrow's path on the far side of the river.

days.t: Day walk to Ama Dablam Base Camp
days.note: Drop to the bridge over the Imja Khola below the village, climb steeply onto the ridge opposite and follow it up through juniper and yak pasture to the base camp flat. Allow three to four hours up and two down. Carry food and water for the day and start back by one.
Back through Deboche and up the short climb to Tengboche, down to Phunki Tenga and up the long hill to the balcony trail. A full day in which most of the effort goes into the two climbs.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Down to the river and out along the valley, with the last climb into Lukla at the end of a long day. Reconfirm your seat with the airline before you sit down to dinner.
Flights to Kathmandu or Manthali leave in the first hours of daylight if the weather holds. If it does not, you wait a day, share a helicopter or walk toward the road.
